author: fwyzard
body: #### PR description: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently, while handing them to the framework in input order. Builds on #52144 (`cms::adler32` with zlib), which is included in this branch and should be merged first. `StreamerInputSource` event deserialization is split into a thread-safe decode step (Adler-32 check, uncompression, ROOT deserialization into per-event buffers) and a serial finish step (meta data check, process history, run and lumi auxiliaries). `StreamerFileReader` reads up to `numDecodeTasks` events ahead and decodes them in TBB tasks; whoever claims an event first decodes it, its task or the source, so while events are being processed the source never waits on a `task_group` or runs unrelated tasks. End of file, new event meta data and read errors are handled serially, after all the events read before them have been handed out, so errors keep their input order. New untracked parameter `numDecodeTasks`: `1` (default) keeps the current serial behaviour; `N > 1` reads up to N events ahead; `0` uses one slot per framework stream. Each event read ahead keeps its message copy, uncompression buffer and deserialized products in memory until the framework takes it, so with `0` the input products need roughly one more copy per stream. Throughput of an input-only job (`GenericConsumer` on all products), 8 threads, AMD EPYC 9534: - 1 MB raw-data events (ZSTD): ~495 ev/s serial, ~2100 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks = 0`; up to ~5000 ev/s with more threads. - 29 kB scouting events: ~2400 ev/s serial, ~8000 ev/s with `numDecodeTasks = 0`; up to ~13000 ev/s. - Run-3 HLT menu on raw-data streamer input, 62 threads: unchanged (~197 ev/s), as the source is not the bottleneck there. #### Performance for Phase 2 HLT inputs (TTbar, pileup 200, skimmed) _Compression time vs compressed file size_ _Read throughput vs file size_ _Peak memory usage vs read throughput_ #### Notes: - The performance of `NewEventStreamFileReader` includes the `adler32` optimisation from #52144. - `DQMStreamerReader` and `StreamerInputModule` (used by `WatcherSource`) are not changed: they keep decoding events serially through `deserializeEvent()`, which now calls the new protected `decodeEvent()`/`finishEvent()`. The only internal change is that the `TBufferFile` read buffer is now created per event instead of being a reused member, which costs almost nothing. They could adopt the pipelined decoding in a follow-up. - Skipping events that were already read ahead (`skip()` with a non-empty window) is covered by review only: `skipEvents` is applied before anything is read ahead, and `processingMode = "RunsAndLumis"`, which skips events one by one, already loops forever with `NewEventStreamFileReader` in the release, independently of this PR. - `RefCoreStreamerGuard` resets the thread-local product getter to `nullptr` instead of restoring the previous value; this PR adds a new way to reach that path, but see #52165. #### PR validation: - New unit test `TestIOPoolStreamerPipelined`: serial vs pipelined (`numDecodeTasks` 16 and 0, 1 and 4 threads) on two files, a file with a meta data change in the middle, a file with repeated meta data, `skipEvents`, a truncated last event and a corrupted checksum; with one thread the failing jobs process all the earlier events, as in serial mode. - All `IOPool/Streamer`, `DQMServices/StreamerIO` and `CalibCalorimetry/EcalLaserSorting` unit tests pass. - Re-writing the events with `EventStreamFileWriter` gives byte-identical output with one thread, and the same set of messages with 16 threads, for raw-data and scouting inputs. title: Make `NewEventStreamFileReader` able to read events ahead and decode them concurrently
